reuse.why: All providers, including the new Fintegra link, go through one assertBankAccountNotLinked guard and the existing linkBankSyncAccount / link.findOrCreateBank helpers; the takeover path, however, rewrites the unlink field-clearing instead of reusing it.

duplication.why: The sync-field reset in the takeover branch copies the db.updateAccount block of unlinkAccount, and downloadFintegraTransactions is a near-copy of downloadAkahuTransactions.

placement.why: Guards are called at the start of each link function, which fits, but a function named assert...NotLinked now also checks the closed-account rule and performs a write (clearing another account's link), mixing validation and mutation.

scope.why: Everything serves the four steps (one-link rule, Fintegra sync, closed accounts, takeover); no unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: Single entry point per provider is good, but the guard has grown a mode flag and a mutating branch, and the copied reset and download code will drift from their originals.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The replaceExistingLink branch in assertBankAccountNotLinked clears the old account's sync fields with its own db.updateAccount instead of going through unlinkAccount (deliberately, to skip GoCardless provider cleanup).

disguised_duplication.where: The copied blocks (unlink field reset, Fintegra download) are near-verbatim, not reshaped.

abstraction_drift.where: assertBankAccountNotLinked gains a replaceExistingLink parameter, a takeover branch that mutates the existing account, and a closed-account check unrelated to its name; every link function calls it, so no call site bypasses it.
